claims.text: Zafirlukast: competitive inhibitor of leukotrienes D4 and E4.
claims.quote: Zafirlukast is a leukotriene receptor antagonist that is a competitive inhibitor of leukotrienes D4 and E4.

claims.text: Zileuton: inhibits 5-lipoxygenase.
claims.quote: Zileuton inhibits 5-lipoxygenase.

claims.text: Asthma: oral long-term control in mild to severe persistent asthma;
claims.quote: Leukotriene receptor antagonists are taken orally and can be used for long-term control and prevention of symptoms in patients with mild persistent to severe persistent asthma.

claims.text: not for an acute attack.
claims.quote: SINGULAIR is not indicated for the treatment of an acute asthma attack.

claims.text: Montelukast: weigh neuropsychiatric risk first, especially when symptoms are mild and other therapies work.
claims.quote: Because of the risk of NP events, the benefits of SINGULAIR may not outweigh the risks in some patients, particularly when the symptoms of disease may be mild and adequately treated with alternative therapies.

claims.text: Montelukast (≥ 15 y) 10 mg
claims.quote: | Adult and adolescent patients 15 years of age and older | one 10 mg tablet

claims.text: once daily in the evening.
claims.quote: For asthma, administer SINGULAIR orally once daily in the evening, with or without food.

claims.text: Zafirlukast (≥ 12 y) 20 mg twice daily,
claims.quote: The recommended dose of zafirlukast in adults and children 12 years and older is 20 mg twice daily.

claims.text: ≥ 1 h before or 2 h after meals.
claims.quote: Because food can reduce the bioavailability of zafirlukast, zafirlukast should be taken at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals.

claims.text: Zileuton 600 mg four times daily (2400 mg/day).
claims.quote: The recommended dosage of ZYFLO for the symptomatic treatment of patients with asthma is one 600-mg tablet four times a day for a total daily dose of 2400 mg.

claims.text: Montelukast boxed warning: serious neuropsychiatric events (agitation, aggression, depression, sleep disturbance, suicidal thoughts/behavior).
claims.quote: Serious neuropsychiatric (NP) events have been reported with the use of SINGULAIR. The types of events reported were highly variable, and included, but were not limited to, agitation, aggression, depression, sleep disturbances, suicidal thoughts and behavior (including suicide).

claims.text: Liver enzyme elevation (mainly zileuton);
claims.quote: The main adverse effect is liver enzyme elevation (which occurs primarily with zileuton).

claims.text: zafirlukast: life-threatening hepatic failure reported.
claims.quote: Cases of life-threatening hepatic failure have been reported in patients treated with zafirlukast.

claims.text: Rare EGPA (Churg-Strauss)-like syndrome,
claims.quote: Although rare, patients have developed a clinical syndrome resembling eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

claims.text: sometimes as oral steroids are reduced.
claims.quote: These events have been sometimes associated with the reduction of oral corticosteroid therapy

claims.text: Zafirlukast: contraindicated in hepatic impairment, including cirrhosis.
claims.quote: Zafirlukast is contraindicated in patients with hepatic impairment including hepatic cirrhosis.

claims.text: Zileuton: contraindicated in active liver disease or transaminases ≥ 3× ULN.
claims.quote: Active liver disease or transaminase elevations greater than or equal to three times the upper limit of normal (≥3xULN)

claims.text: Zileuton roughly doubles theophylline levels (reduce theophylline, monitor levels),
claims.quote: Co-administration of ZYFLO and theophylline results in, on average, an approximate doubling of serum theophylline concentrations. Theophylline dosage in these patients should be reduced and serum theophylline concentrations monitored closely

claims.text: raises PT with warfarin,
claims.quote: Co-administration of ZYFLO and warfarin results in a clinically significant increase in prothrombin time (PT).

claims.text: and doubles propranolol exposure.
claims.quote: Co-administration of ZYFLO and propranolol results in doubling of propranolol AUC and consequent increased beta-blocker activity.

claims.text: Zafirlukast raises S-warfarin exposure and PT (~35%);
claims.quote: resulted in a significant increase in the mean AUC (+63%) and half-life (+36%) of S-warfarin. The mean prothrombin time increased by approximately 35%.

claims.text: erythromycin lowers zafirlukast levels (~40%).
claims.quote: Coadministration of a single dose of zafirlukast (40 mg) with erythromycin (500 mg three times daily for 5 days) to steady-state in 11 asthmatic patients resulted in decreased mean plasma concentrations of zafirlukast by approximately 40%

claims.text: Zileuton: ALT before starting, monthly × 3 months, every two to three months for the rest of the first year, then periodically; stop if liver symptoms or transaminases > 5× ULN.
claims.quote: Serum ALT should be monitored before treatment begins, once-a-month for the first 3 months, every two to three months for the remainder of the first year, and periodically thereafter for patients receiving long-term ZYFLO therapy. If clinical signs and/or symptoms of liver dysfunction (e.g., right upper quadrant pain, nausea, fatigue, lethargy, pruritus, jaundice, or “flu-like” symptoms) develop or transaminase elevations greater than 5 times the ULN occur, ZYFLO should be discontinued

claims.text: Montelukast: watch for behavior/mood changes; stop and call the prescriber if new neuropsychiatric symptoms or suicidal thoughts occur.
claims.quote: Advise patients and/or caregivers to be alert for changes in behavior or new NP symptoms when taking SINGULAIR. If changes in behavior are observed, or if new NP symptoms or suicidal thoughts and/or behavior occur, advise patients to discontinue SINGULAIR and contact a healthcare provider immediately

claims.text: Keep a SABA for rescue.
claims.quote: All patients should have available for rescue a short-acting β-agonist.
